meta.purpose: Single source of truth so the developer and any AI coding assistant build exactly the same application. If code and this file disagree, ask the owner before deciding.

language_policy.ui_language: Indonesian (id-ID). All user-facing copy is Indonesian. Keep all UI strings in one i18n file (messages/id.json) so English can be added later.

how_ai_should_use_this_file: Read the whole file before generating code for any feature.
Implement only what is marked for the current phase (see roadmap). Do not build later-phase features unless asked.
Anything listed in open_decisions is NOT decided. Do not invent an answer: use the stated default or ask the owner.
Business rules in business_rules and pricing_calculation are mandatory and must be enforced on the server.
Follow ai_coder_rules at the bottom of this file for every task.
Items marked [ASSUMPTION] were proposed by the planner and are awaiting owner confirmation.
For any UI work, also read docs/design/DESIGN.md completely and pass its review checklist (section 14). It overrides this file on visual decisions.

id_conventions.phases: 0 = preparation, 1 = MVP, 2 = growth features, 3 = polish and scale

project.name: Care Care
project.previous_working_name: NEO // THREADS (deprecated, do not use in code, UI, or copy)
project.type: Single-store e-commerce website (NOT a multi-vendor marketplace)
project.target_audience: Young Indonesian shoppers (Gen Z and young millennials), mostly on mobile phones
project.currency_rules: Store money as integer rupiah (no decimals, no floats). Format as 'Rp 160.000'.
project.timestamps: Store in UTC. Display in the store timezone configured in admin settings (default Asia/Jakarta, owner can change).
project.catalog_size: Dynamic. The owner adds, edits, and removes products via the admin panel. Never hardcode products.
project.one_line_summary: Care Care is a single-owner online clothing store with dynamic catalog and variant-level stock, 15-minute payment window, buyer-paid payment fees, real-time courier rates across Indonesia, and one admin panel for the owner.

logo.file_status: Provided as PNG (Frame_1.png). SVG version needed for production.
required_variants: icon-only for favicon and app icon
horizontal lockup with wordmark CARE CARE

design_style.name: Kotak dan Lipatan (Grid and Fold): neo-brutalism built from the Care Care logo
principles: Catalog is a lattice of cells sharing 2px ink borders, not separate rounded cards.
Border thickness encodes hierarchy: 3px primary, 2px interactive, 1px data dividers.
Radius 0 everywhere except pill stickers and status pills.
Hard offset shadows only on pressable elements.
45-degree chamfer on large blocks (max two per screen). Wishlist is a folded page corner (dog-ear).
Woven check motif only in: sold-out overlay, footer band, 404/empty states, payment success.
One badge per product. No gradients, glass blur, or stock illustration.
Motion only as response to user action, plus one logo-assembly moment on first home load per session.
improvements_over_reference_design: Maximum one badge per product card.
Body and description text never below 14px.
Primary CTA is large, filled terracotta or navy, high contrast, never small white.
Navigation text is large enough and has clear hover, focus, and active states.
Every product, including accessories, shows price and a quick add action.
No placeholder text or typos in production.
Filters, sorting, ratings, and size selection exist in the catalog and product detail.
design_style.badge_rule: SOLD_OUT overrides any other badge. Otherwise at most one badge is shown, chosen by the admin per product.
design_style.badge_style: pill sticker, rotated up to 3 degrees, gold background with ink text; SOLD_OUT uses ink background with white text. No starburst shapes.

Track an order using order number plus email or phone

tech_stack.principle: One language (TypeScript), one repository, popular and well-documented tools, managed hosting.
tech_stack.styling: Tailwind CSS v4. Design tokens in app/globals.css via @theme (tailwind.config.ts only if the project uses v3). Tokens defined in DESIGN.md section 13.
tech_stack.ui_components: shadcn/ui as a base only. Every component must be overridden to DESIGN.md (radius 0, ink borders, hard shadows). Icons: Lucide with square caps and miter joins.
tech_stack.orm: Prisma 7 with @prisma/adapter-pg (works for local Postgres and Neon)
tech_stack.auth: Auth.js v5 (next-auth@beta) with @auth/prisma-adapter. Credentials login requires JWT session strategy.
tech_stack.image_upload: Cloudinary or UploadThing (auto resize and optimization)
tech_stack.scheduled_jobs: Vercel Cron (or equivalent) for expiring reservations and auto-completing orders
tech_stack.bot_protection: Cloudflare Turnstile (or reCAPTCHA) on register, login, checkout
tech_stack.versions_note: Next.js 16 (middleware.ts is renamed proxy.ts), Auth.js v5 installed as next-auth@beta, Prisma 7 (requires a driver adapter, prisma.config.ts, generated client in project folder, Node 20.19+ or 22.12+ or 24+). Verify current versions when starting.
tech_stack.containerization: None. Docker is not used. Do not generate Dockerfile or docker-compose files unless the owner asks.

database_environments.approach: One Neon project with separate branches per environment.

branches.main: production database (used only by the live site)
branches.dev: development database (used on the developer machine, can be reset and reseeded freely)
branches.test: automated tests database (optional, created when e2e tests are added)

connection_strings.DATABASE_URL: Pooled connection string, used by the running application.
connection_strings.DIRECT_URL: Direct (non-pooled) connection string, used only by Prisma CLI for migrations.

rules: Never run experiments or seeds against the production branch.
Migrations are created on dev, committed to Git, then applied to production with prisma migrate deploy during release.
Production DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL exist only in the hosting provider environment settings, never on the developer machine.
database_environments.alternative_if_neon_unavailable: Install PostgreSQL directly on the machine (no Docker). Use the same variable names.

project_structure.layering: UI components must not call integrations directly. Flow: UI -> server action or route handler -> service layer in lib/ -> Prisma/integration clients.

products.dynamic_catalog: All products, categories, variants, images, prices, banners, collections are managed in admin and stored in the database.
products.variant_model: Every product has at least one variant. A simple product without options gets one default variant. Variants are combinations of options such as Size x Color.
products.stock_level: Stock is stored and enforced PER VARIANT. Product total stock is DERIVED as the sum of its active variants (shown in admin lists and used for product-level SOLD OUT).
products.sold_out_behavior: When a variant stock is 0 it shows as unavailable in the selector. When all variants are 0 the product shows SOLD OUT and add-to-bag is disabled.
products.low_stock: Admin dashboard lists variants at or below low_stock_threshold (default 5, editable in settings).
products.badges: Admin picks at most one badge per product from badge_enum.
products.slug: Unique, lowercase, URL-safe, auto-generated from name and editable.
products.soft_delete: Products with order history are archived, never hard-deleted.

drops.description: A Collection can be of type DROP with drop_starts_at and optional drop_ends_at. Before start, the page shows a countdown and buying is disabled (server-enforced). After start, normal purchase. Optional per-customer purchase limit per drop.
drops.server_enforcement: Never rely on the client clock. Check drop time on the server at add-to-cart and at checkout.

cart.guest_cart: Stored server-side with a cookie session id (or client storage for MVP simplicity). Merged into the customer cart on login.
rules: Quantity cannot exceed available stock of the variant.
Cart does NOT reserve stock.
Cart page re-validates price and stock every time it loads and shows clear messages for changes.

stock_reservation.why: Prevent overselling when multiple buyers purchase the last items at the same time, especially during drops.
stock_reservation.owner_statement: Stock is locked when the stock entered by the admin has been fully sold.
implementation: Stock reservation happens when the buyer confirms payment (creates the order with PENDING_PAYMENT), not when adding to cart.

Reservation reduces available stock immediately (available = stock - active reservations) inside a database transaction using row locking or an atomic conditional update (UPDATE ... SET stock = stock - qty WHERE stock >= qty). Never read-then-write without protection.
Reservation lasts exactly 15 minutes (payment_window_minutes setting, default 15).
On payment success: reservation becomes a permanent deduction.
On expiry or cancellation before payment: reservation is released and stock returns.
When available stock reaches 0 the variant is automatically shown as SOLD OUT.
stock_reservation.expiry_mechanism: Set Midtrans custom expiry to the same 15 minutes AND run a scheduled job every minute that cancels expired PENDING_PAYMENT orders and releases reservations. Also check expiry lazily when an order is read.
stock_reservation.late_payment_edge_case: If a payment webhook arrives after the order was cancelled for expiry: do not silently revive the order. Mark payment_status as PAID_AFTER_EXPIRY, flag the order in admin for manual decision (restock-check then fulfill, or refund), and notify admin.

statuses.description: Order created, stock reserved, buyer has 15 minutes to pay.
Payment confirmed. Admin prepares and packs the order.
Shipment created, tracking number (resi) issued, with the courier.
Delivered and accepted. Auto-completes N days after delivery (auto_complete_after_delivered_days, default 3) or when the customer confirms receipt.
Cancelled automatically (payment expired) or manually. Stock restored.
A return request exists for this order. Details are tracked in ReturnRequest.

transition_rules: Customer may cancel only while PENDING_PAYMENT.
Admin may cancel PROCESSING orders (triggers refund flow and restock).
PENDING_PAYMENT -> PROCESSING only through a verified payment webhook, never from the browser.
RETURN -> COMPLETED when the return is rejected. RETURN -> CANCELLED (with refund) when the return is approved and refunded for the full order.
Every status change writes an OrderStatusHistory row (from, to, actor, reason, timestamp) and triggers the matching notification and email.
Invalid transitions must throw an error. Centralize transitions in one function (orderService.transition).

enabled_methods: VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT (BCA, BNI, BRI, Mandiri, Permata, etc. as enabled in Midtrans)
payment.payment_fee_policy: The BUYER pays the payment fee. Show it as its own line in cart summary, checkout, order detail, and invoice before the buyer pays.
payment.payment_fee_calculation: Fee is computed by our server from a configurable table per method (flat amount and/or percentage). The buyer chooses the payment method BEFORE paying, so create the Snap transaction restricted to the chosen method via enabled_payments so the fee shown always matches. Owner must verify the real gateway fee schedule and set the table in admin settings.
security: Payment confirmation comes ONLY from the Midtrans notification webhook.
Verify the webhook signature (SHA512 of order_id + status_code + gross_amount + server key) and then confirm status via the Midtrans status API before changing order state.
Webhook handler must be idempotent (store processed event ids; same event twice changes nothing).
Never store card data. Never log secrets.
payment.midtrans_amount_rule: Midtrans gross_amount must equal the sum of item_details. Send items, shipping, tax, payment fee, and discounts as separate lines (discount as a negative line) so totals match exactly.
payment.account_type_note: Available payment methods can differ between individual and business-entity merchant accounts. Confirm with Midtrans before launch.

shipping.rates: Real-time via Biteship rates endpoint (POST /v1/rates/couriers) using origin postal code, destination postal code, and item list (name, value, weight, quantity).
shipping.couriers: Owner selects the allowed couriers and services in admin settings from what Biteship offers. Default: show all enabled. Exact list is an open decision.
shipping.origin: Single warehouse/origin configured in admin settings (name, address, postal code, phone). [ASSUMPTION: one origin]
weight_rules: Total weight = sum(variant.weight_gram x qty) + packaging_weight_gram (setting).
Minimum chargeable weight 1000 g (setting), as most couriers bill per kg.

free_shipping.description: Rule-based, configurable in admin. The store absorbs the discounted amount.
free_shipping.also_via_voucher: A voucher of type FREE_SHIPPING can grant it.

shipping.shipment_creation: Admin clicks 'Kirim' on a PROCESSING order -> backend creates the Biteship order -> store waybill (resi), courier, and label link -> status SHIPPED.
shipping.tracking: Biteship webhooks update shipment status. Customer sees a tracking timeline. Handle webhook events for status, price change, and waybill id. Webhook handler is idempotent.
shipping.price_change_risk: If the courier reprices because actual weight differs, record the difference (shipping_adjustment) on the shipment and show it in admin finance. Accurate variant weight is therefore mandatory.
shipping.insurance: Optional per courier. Default policy is an open decision.

returns_and_refunds.note: Default general policy proposed by the planner, editable by the owner. [ASSUMPTION]
returns_and_refunds.wrong_size_policy: Size exchange only, subject to stock. Return shipping paid by the customer.
returns_and_refunds.item_condition: Unused, unwashed, tags and original packaging intact.
returns_and_refunds.evidence: Unboxing video or photos are required for WRONG_ITEM, DEFECTIVE, DAMAGED_IN_SHIPPING.
returns_and_refunds.non_returnable: Products flagged is_final_sale and hygiene-sensitive accessories (admin flag per product).
returns_and_refunds.return_shipping_cost: Store pays if the store is at fault (WRONG_ITEM, DEFECTIVE, DAMAGED_IN_SHIPPING, NOT_AS_DESCRIBED). Customer pays for WRONG_SIZE or personal reasons.
returns_and_refunds.refund: To the original payment method (via payment gateway or manual transfer decided by admin) or store credit voucher. Target 3 to 14 business days after the item passes inspection.
returns_and_refunds.warranty: Manufacturing defects within 7 to 14 days of delivery.
returns_and_refunds.restock_rule: Admin decides per returned item whether to restock after inspection.

vouchers.validation: Always validated on the server at cart, at checkout, and again at order creation. A voucher use is counted when the order is created and released if the order expires or is cancelled.

reviews.who_can_review: Customers with a COMPLETED order that contains the item. One review per order item.
reviews.content: Rating 1 to 5, text, up to 3 photos.
reviews.moderation: Published immediately, admin can hide or delete. Admin can reply publicly. Reported reviews flagged. [ASSUMPTION: post-moderation]
reviews.display: Average rating and count on product cards and detail page.

accounts_and_data.address_book: Customers can save multiple addresses with one default. Address includes recipient name, phone, province, city, district, postal code (needed for rates), full address, notes.
accounts_and_data.account_deletion: Customer can request deletion and data export (UU PDP rights). Order records needed for tax/accounting are retained in anonymized form.

pricing_calculation.owner_requirement: Total must include goods, shipping, tax, and fees, calculated consistently everywhere.
pricing_calculation.single_source_of_truth: lib/pricing/calculateOrderTotal.ts. Used by cart, checkout, order creation, and admin. No other place may compute totals.
formula: voucher_discount = computed from voucher rules (never more than subtotal)
shipping_cost = rate returned by Biteship for the chosen courier service
shipping_discount = free shipping rule or FREE_SHIPPING voucher, capped at shipping_cost
taxable_base = subtotal - voucher_discount (+ shipping_cost - shipping_discount if the owner decides shipping is taxable)
tax = if tax.enabled then rate x taxable_base (if prices are tax-exclusive) or the tax portion already inside prices (if tax-inclusive), else 0
payment_fee = lookup by chosen payment method from fee table
grand_total = subtotal - voucher_discount + shipping_cost - shipping_discount + tax(if exclusive) + payment_fee
pricing_calculation.rounding: Compute in integer rupiah. Round each line using the same rounding function (round half up) and document it. Totals must never be off by 1 rupiah between screens.

tax_settings.enabled: false by default until the owner confirms PKP/PPN status
tax_settings.rate_percent: Configurable in admin. Do not hardcode. Confirm current rate with a tax consultant.

pricing_calculation.snapshot_rule: At order creation, copy into the order: item names, SKUs, unit prices, quantities, voucher code and discount, shipping service and cost, tax rate and amount, payment fee, grand_total. Later price or setting changes must never alter existing orders.
pricing_calculation.server_only: The client may display an estimate but the server recalculates everything at order creation and rejects mismatches or uses the server value.

flows: Create Snap transaction restricted to chosen method with 15 minute expiry
Verify signature and status, update Payment and Order
Refund via API or manual (decide per method)

biteship.area_data: Address forms need province, city, district, postal code. Use Biteship maps/area lookup or a local area dataset, so postal code is always valid.

cloudinary_or_uploadthing.use: Product, banner, review, and return evidence images
rules: Max 5 MB per image
jpg, png, webp
Generate responsive sizes
Store public id and URL

auth_google.note: Auth.js v5 reads AUTH_* variables. NEXTAUTH_* names are legacy.

webhook_rules: Respond fast with 200 after persisting the event.
Store raw event in WebhookEvent table for audit and idempotency.
Handle retries and out-of-order events safely.

data_model.note: Conceptual model for Prisma. Types are indicative. All tables have id, created_at, updated_at unless stated. Money = Int (IDR). Add indexes on foreign keys, slug, sku, order_number, status, created_at.

StockMovement: reason enum(MANUAL_ADJUST, SALE, CANCEL_RESTOCK, RETURN_RESTOCK, INITIAL)
Order: status enum(PENDING_PAYMENT, PROCESSING, SHIPPED, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, RETURN)

critical_constraints: Stock changes only through stockService so every change writes a StockMovement.
Order items and prices are snapshots, never joined live for historical display.

storefront.description: Enter order number plus email or phone to view status and tracking.

account_and_auth.description: Email+password and Google. Password rules min 8 chars. Bot protection. Rate limiting. Verification email.

account_and_auth.name: Forgot and reset password
account_and_auth.description: Signed, single-use, expiring (e.g. 30 minutes) token via email.

account_and_auth.description: List with status filter, detail with items and totals, payment instructions while pending, countdown to expiry, tracking timeline, invoice view/print.

checkout.name: Payment page
checkout.description: Shows payment instructions per method (VA number, e-wallet deeplink, QRIS), amount, 15-minute countdown, auto-refresh/poll status, 'change payment method' only if allowed by gateway (otherwise new order flow), expired and failed states.

checkout.name: Order confirmation
checkout.description: Success page and email with summary.

admin.name: Admin dashboard
admin.description: Today and period sales, orders by status, new orders needing processing, low stock list, top products, simple revenue chart.

admin.name: Product management
admin.description: List with search, filter, status, stock total. Create/edit with images upload and reorder, options and variants generator (size x color), per-variant price, stock, weight, SKU, badge (max one), category, SEO, final-sale flag, draft/active/archive. Bulk stock edit. Stock adjustment with reason (StockMovement).

admin.name: Order management
admin.description: List with filters (status, date, payment method, search by number/name). Detail: items, customer, address, payment, timeline. Actions: mark packed, create shipment (resi), print shipping label and packing slip, cancel with reason, add admin note. Real-time or near real-time new order indicator.

admin.name: Returns and refunds management
admin.description: Review requests and evidence, approve or reject with reason, mark item received, decide restock, record refund, update status.

admin.name: Customer management
admin.description: List, detail with order history and total spent, block or unblock.

admin.description: Create and manage vouchers per business_rules.vouchers.

admin.name: Content management
admin.description: Articles, FAQ, static pages with rich text editor.

admin.description: Sales report by period, payment method breakdown, shipping cost vs charged, payment fees collected, tax collected, refunds. Export CSV.

payment: fee table per method (type flat|percent, value)
returns: policy text shortcut to static page

requirements: HTTPS everywhere, secure and httpOnly cookies, SameSite lax or strict.
Hash passwords with bcrypt or argon2.
Authorization checks on every server action and route handler. Never rely on hiding buttons.
Customers can only access their own orders, addresses, returns, and reviews (ownership checks).
Validate every input with Zod on the server. Sanitize rich text (articles, product descriptions).
Rate limit login, register, forgot password, voucher validation, checkout creation, contact form.
Bot protection on register, login, checkout, contact.
Verify all webhook signatures. Idempotent processing.
Admin routes under /admin protected by proxy.ts (Next.js 16 name for middleware) plus per-action permission checks.
Do not expose internal ids where order_number is enough. Do not leak whether an email exists on forgot password.
Secrets only in environment variables. Never commit .env.
Database backups (provider automated daily) and tested restore procedure.
Upload validation: type, size, and scan names. Serve through the image CDN.
Audit log for sensitive admin actions: price change, stock adjust, cancel, refund, settings change, staff change.

performance: Use Next.js Image with CDN-optimized images and defined sizes.
Static or incremental static generation for home, catalog pages, product pages, collections, articles. Revalidate on admin change.
Cart, checkout, account, admin are dynamic.
Database indexes on slug, sku, status, category_id, created_at, order_number.
Drop-day protection: atomic stock updates, rate limiting, cached read-only catalog, avoid N+1 queries.
Target Lighthouse mobile performance 85+ on home and product pages.
seo: Clean slugs, canonical URLs, unique title and meta description per page.
Product JSON-LD structured data (name, image, price, availability, rating).

rules: Color contrast at least 4.5:1 for normal text.
Visible focus states on all interactive elements.
Full keyboard navigation for menus, drawers, modals, filters.
Alt text for all product images (admin field).
Form labels and error messages linked to inputs.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion for rotated stickers, marquee, and countdown animations.
Touch targets at least 44x44px.
mobile_notes: Sticky add-to-bag bar on product detail.

ai_coder_rules: Language: TypeScript strict. No 'any' unless justified with a comment.
All money is integer IDR. Never use floating point for money.
All price, stock, voucher, shipping, tax, and fee calculations happen on the server using lib/pricing and services. Never trust client-supplied totals.
Stock changes only through stockService inside a database transaction with an atomic conditional update. Always create a StockMovement.
Order status changes only through orderService.transition which enforces allowed_transitions and writes OrderStatusHistory.
Payment and shipping state changes come only from verified, idempotent webhooks (plus status API verification for payments).
Use Zod schemas shared by form and server validation.
Check authentication and authorization (role, permission, ownership) in every server action and route handler.
UI copy is Indonesian. Code, comments, commits, and identifiers are English.
Every data-driven view needs loading (skeleton), empty, and error states.
Never log secrets, tokens, or full payment payloads containing personal data in client logs.
Write unit tests for pricing, stock, voucher, and status transitions before wiring them into UI.
Keep functions small, name things by domain terms used in this file (Order, Variant, Reservation, Shipment, ReturnRequest).
When something is unclear or marked open, stop and ask the owner instead of guessing. Record the answer by updating this file.
Update this spec file in the same commit whenever behavior changes.
Follow docs/design/DESIGN.md for every visual decision and run its review checklist (section 14) before finishing any UI task.
Never use default Tailwind colors, rounded-* (except rounded-full on stickers and pills), shadow-sm/md/lg/xl, gradients, or backdrop-blur. Use design tokens and messages/id.json only.
Do not invent brand copy or a tagline. Use messages/id.json and ask the owner (DESIGN.md DD-05).
